sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Arsenal host Bournemouth at Emirates Stadium with top spot (70 points) on the line, while the visitors sit 13th (42 points). Sofascore’s model leans to a home win (63%) over a draw (20%) or away win (17%), with a 59% chance that both teams score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Arsenal are 3-0-2 across their last 5, with 3 clean sheets and strong shot output (34 shots on target in that run). Bournemouth are unbeaten in 5 but winless (0-5-0), solid defensively (3 clean sheets) yet wasteful in attack, missing several big chances in multiple matches.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Arsenal won the reverse fixture in January, but Bournemouth won at the Emirates last season. Both recent meetings saw both teams score, and the broader matchup trend has produced open games.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and tactical notes
sections.text: Arsenal lead the league for goals scored (61) and least conceded (22), press high effectively (possessions won in the final third rank 1) and allow the fewest shots (7.8 per match). Bournemouth’s goal difference is near even (46-48) and they score late relatively often, showing resilience in long spells.

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: Declan Rice drives Arsenal’s creativity (59 key passes, 14 big chances created) and Gabriel Magalhães dominates duels (76% ground duels won). For Bournemouth, Marcos Senesi’s distribution is key and Eli Junior Kroupi (9 goals) offers a threat, though recent finishing across the team has been inconsistent.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Michael Oliver averages 3.5 yellow cards and 0.14 red cards per match. Arsenal are disciplined (1.29 yellows per game; fewest in the league) and recent meetings trend to low card counts. Corners should be healthy given Arsenal’s 5.8 per match and Bournemouth’s recent average close to 6.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Arsenal are favoured and their defensive control plus home advantage should tell, but Bournemouth’s 10-match unbeaten run suggests they can create moments. A home win with both teams likely to score fits the data and the model lean.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal and Bournemouth are level at half-time (1-1) at Emirates Stadium. Eli Junior Kroupi opened the scoring on 17 minutes from open play, before Viktor Gyökeres equalised from the penalty spot on 35 minutes. The numbers point to a balanced contest with different strengths: Arsenal lead on expected goals (1.26–0.71) and big chances (2–1), while Bournemouth edge shots on target (2–1), final-third entries (25–18) and penalty-area entries (14–10). Possession is near even (49–51). Bournemouth have the aerial edge (64% won) but Arsenal have the broader duels advantage (53%). Corners are 3–0 to Arsenal.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal started with control and territory, but Bournemouth threatened in transition and struck first through Kroupi. Arsenal responded with sustained pressure and earned a penalty that Gyökeres converted. The half finished with Bournemouth pushing Arsenal back, forcing several defensive actions inside the box. Overall: Arsenal have created the better quality chances, Bournemouth have generated more entries and direct threat.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal were on top in the opening phase before Bournemouth enjoyed a productive spell around the opening goal. Arsenal then built a strong period surrounding the equaliser, with pressure sustained for several minutes. Bournemouth finished the half with their best attacking sequence, stringing together multiple waves before the whistle.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal’s structure has Rice advancing to connect play and find runners, with Ben White stepping high and wide players looking for cut-backs rather than aerial crosses given the first-half aerial deficit. Bournemouth are compact and quick to release wide, with Tavernier and Kroupi attacking space and Evanilson offering a direct outlet. Bournemouth’s success in the air and on second balls has underpinned their transitions and late-half pressure.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key player notes
halftimeSections.text: Declan Rice has been the most influential Arsenal player (rating 7.6), creating 1 big chance and 1 key pass. Kai Havertz has 0.40 expected goals and 1 big chance missed. Viktor Gyökeres has 1 shot on target and 0.79 expected goals, driven by the penalty. For Bournemouth, Kroupi has 0.66 expected goals and the goal, while James Hill (rating 7.0) leads the defence with 3 clearances. Ryan Christie’s work rate (2 tackles, 2 interceptions) has supported Bournemouth’s pressing and cover.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Adjustments for the second half
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal should keep combinations on the floor, use underlapping runs to find cut-backs, and attack the channels behind the full-backs rather than playing aerial balls into crowded areas. Earlier service to Gyökeres’ feet and more third-man runs from Havertz can stress Bournemouth’s centre-backs. Bournemouth can continue to target turnovers and quick diagonals into Evanilson, while maintaining width for Kroupi and Tavernier. With their aerial edge, Bournemouth should attack wide free-kicks and long throws, but must manage fouls around their own box given Arsenal’s territory.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline and set pieces
halftimeSections.text: Cards: none shown in the first half. Expect a tighter whistle after the break with 3–4 yellow cards overall and no red cards anticipated. Corners: Arsenal lead 3–0 at the interval; the pattern suggests Arsenal to finish ahead on corners, projected around 7–4. Set-piece threat: Arsenal’s sustained pressure should yield more dead-ball situations, while Bournemouth’s aerial strength makes them dangerous on wide deliveries.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Bournemouth ended the half on the front foot, but Arsenal’s chance quality and control phases point to a strong response after the restart. If Arsenal increase the tempo and keep the game on the ground, they are well placed to create the next clear chance. Bournemouth remain live on transitions and set-pieces, so defensive rest defence for Arsenal will be crucial.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Edge to Arsenal after the interval. Next goal: Arsenal. Likely scorer: Viktor Gyökeres. Predicted final score: 2–1 Arsenal, with a single goal after half-time.
